beats.hook: I walked out of my job mid-shift — and I took something with me that made my manager's face go completely white.
beats.the_wrong: For eight months, my manager Diane had been stealing my sales commissions. She'd reassign my closed deals to herself right before payroll processed — and HR told me there was "nothing to investigate."
beats.the_plan: So I stopped reporting my closes to the system. I let them stack up — undocumented, unassigned, invisible. I was waiting for the right moment.
beats.the_execution: On a Friday afternoon — our busiest shift — I opened the shared drive. I copied every piece of documentation proving those deals were mine. Dates, client emails, call recordings. Months of it. Then I printed it all out, set it on Diane's keyboard, and walked to her office door. I said, "I quit. Also — accounting just got a copy of that." Her face dropped. She actually reached for the papers before I was even out the door.
beats.the_satisfaction: By Monday, two other reps had come forward with the same complaint against her. I heard she was put on a formal investigation within the week. Would you have waited as long as I did — or would you have blown it up sooner?
beats.cta: Drop a comment: did I play it right, or did I let her off too easy for too long?
